State mobilization is active and additional resources are en route. The Tucannon Fire is the largest active zero-containment fire in the current PNW wave and lands on Independence Day weekend with maximum recreational-vehicle ignition risk and reduced agency staffing. items.headline: Russia Fuel Crisis Day 5 — Ukraine Drones Disable 25-33% Russian Refining Capacity; IEA Calls Disruption 'Unprecedented'; 56+ Regions Fuel Restrictions; Moscow Queues; India Offers Supply; Kstovo Lukoil Fire July 2
items.summary: The Russia Fuel Crisis enters Day 5 as Ukrainian drone strikes have now disabled approximately 25-33% of Russia's total oil refining capacity. Russian crude processing fell to approximately 3.95 million barrels per day in June — roughly 25% below the prior year — while gasoline production dropped to approximately 850,000 barrels per day from more than 1 million barrels per year earlier. The visible domestic impact is severe: long queues at petrol stations are now a common sight across Russia including Moscow, at least 56 Russian regions have introduced fuel restrictions, and Russian-installed authorities in Crimea imposed a ban on public fuel sales with only emergency and military vehicles permitted to fill up. The Kremlin is taking the extraordinary step of looking outside the country for supply — Indian Minister of Petroleum Hardeep Singh Puri stated India was ready to support Russia with oil and gas supply. The most recent acute escalation: on July 2, Ukrainian drones attacked the Kstovsky Lukoil refinery (Nizhegorodnefteorgsintez), sparking a major fire at the AVT-6 primary oil refinery unit. Putin acknowledged the shortage publicly (June 29 CNBC reporting). The IEA has characterized the refining supply disruption as 'unprecedented.' This crisis is unfolding simultaneously with the post-Hormuz oil market normalization — the two supply-side events interact: Russia's refining crisis tightens global refined product supply (gasoline, diesel) even as Hormuz crude normalization is easing crude prices. Net effect: divergence between crude oil trajectory ($67-68, declining) and refined product pricing (upward pressure from Russian refinery losses).

US tone remains constructive: Trump characterized denuclearization as 'moving along well' following Doha mediator meetings, with Vance characterizing discussions as 'going well' and envoys Witkoff and Kushner meeting Qatari Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani. Structural friction continues: IAEA has not been granted access to Natanz, Isfahan, and Fordow bombed enrichment sites — no inspection since February 28, 2026. US and Iranian leadership continue contradicting each other in public about MOU meaning, signaling persistent interpretive gaps at the principal level. Hormuz commercial normalization continues: UAE exports restored to 3.9+ million barrels per day, Saudi Arabia ramping Asia exports, total Hormuz daily flows above 10 million barrels. WTI at $67-68, well below pre-deal range. CISA at Day 65 clean; Shamkhani cyber window Day 42 in retaliation-opportunism profile — no confirmed incident.

items.headline: OBBB Law Day 6 (Signed June 30) — $1.4T in Mandatory Cuts Enacted; June Jobs 57K Miss (Released July 2); Dow Record ~52,900; Monday July 7 First Full Session with Full Picture
items.summary: The One Big Beautiful Bill (OBBB/Reconciliation 2.0) was signed into law on June 30, 2026 — Law Day 6 entering July 5 morning. House passage by a razor-thin margin and Senate passage delivered on the timeline signaled by Speaker Johnson in June. Fiscal architecture: $1.4 trillion in mandatory spending reductions over 10 years (Medicaid work requirements/eligibility restrictions, SNAP eligibility and benefit changes, student loan program restructuring); TCJA 2017 tax cut extension (making individual and business cuts permanent); CBO estimates +$3.4 trillion deficit increase versus current-law baseline; Republicans used a current-policy baseline to show a $0.4 trillion reduction. Implementation workstreams are now active at CMS, USDA Food and Nutrition Service, and Department of Education from the June 30 signing date. June Jobs report: June nonfarm payrolls came in at 57K — a significant miss versus expectations — released Thursday July 2 ahead of the Independence Day weekend. Despite the weak print, the Dow Jones Industrial Average reached a record approximately 52,900 in holiday-shortened trading, suggesting equity markets are looking through the labor market deceleration in the context of WTI at $67-68 and Hormuz normalization. Markets closed July 4; Monday July 7 is the first full session where traders process June Jobs miss + Russia refined-product supply disruption + OBBB enacted in combination.

CIDRAP slowing signal advances to Day 29, the longest sustained deceleration of the 2026 arc. 41 jurisdictions affected; 93% outbreak-associated; national vaccination coverage at 92.5% (below 95% herd immunity threshold). Georgetown University wastewater and ER surveillance showing no mass-gathering-sourced cluster. Second: SNSC nuclear compliance Day 17 — the July 4 holiday pause is lifting as of July 5 morning; SNSC is the operative nuclear compliance monitoring mechanism tracking from MOU signing June 19. The July 5 day will be the first post-holiday SNSC compliance check. Third: acting DNI vacancy at Day 45, carrying sustained maximum nuclear verification load — 60-day clock requires ongoing IC assessment of Iranian HEU inventory, enrichment centrifuge status, and IRGC stand-down compliance. Fourth: SCOTUS term is concluding — major rulings on executive power, birthright citizenship, and election law may issue during the July term closing period.

Georgetown University wastewater surveillance shows no mass-gathering-sourced signal. The immediate post-FIFA mass-gathering risk window is closed; next measles surveillance focus shifts to school-year pre-positioning (late July, early August). Third: NSF Newport OR ocean observatories removal is confirmed complete at approximately June 28. Cascadia Subduction Zone real-time offshore monitoring gap is now in its second week of operational status. No federal replacement has been announced. The atmospheric river event forecast for tonight-Wednesday will test land-based seismic and coastal monitoring for any Cascadia slow-slip signals without the offshore early-warning network.
